newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir militants appeal for hostages' release.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir militants appeal for hostages' release.

text.p: Hardcore militants who Indian authorities claim are linked to the kidnapping of Westerners in Kashmir last year appealed on Friday for the release of the four captive tourists.
Harkat-ul-Ansar delivered a statement in Urdu to local newspapers in Srinagar, summer capital of India's Jammu and Kashmir state.

"If any militant group has abducted them as the Indian media is projecting, we appeal to them that if they are true Moslems, for God's sake and for the betterment of Kashmir's freedom movement, they should release them immediately," it said.

The Indian government believes Pakistan-based Harkat-ul-Ansar is linked to shadowy Al-Faran guerrillas who kidnapped American Donald Hutchings, German Dirk Hasert and Britons Paul Wells and Keith Mangan in July 1995.
Norwegian Hans Christian Ostroe, who was also kidnapped by Al-Faran the same month, was later found beheaded.
Harkat-ul-Ansar denies any ties to Al-Faran.
Indian authorities and diplomats say efforts to win the release of the hostages suffered a setback in February when a Harkat commander named Sikender died while handling an explosive device.
On Wednesday, relatives of the American and British hostages visited Sikender's mother.
"We are extremely thankful to hostage families who visited Sikender's house and expressed sympathy with the bereaved family," the Harkat-ul-Ansar statement said.
"We also have every sympathy with them (hostage families), who have travelled thousands of kilometres and reached Kashmir to know the whereabouts of their dear ones," it said.
The statement said the identity of the kidnappers was not known, and that if Indian secret agencies had captured the tourists, it was to discredit the separatist movement in Kashmir.
"We extend all our sympathies to the families. We share their grief and pain. We are with them," it said.

"These tourists are not remotely connected with the ongoing freedom struggle of Kashmir, so the group who has kidnapped these tourists can give proof of the pro-freedom movement of Kashmir by releasing these innocents."
Indian authorities and diplomats say they do not know if the hostages are dead or alive.
